one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings in the window (FQ1 FY27 is mid/late Dec 2026). In the window: (1) the Taiwan labor dispute: Taoyuan/Taichung unions (~10,000 of ~15,000 staff; Taiwan is ~60% of Micron output incl. much HBM) vote on a strike in early October, ~80% backed action, and Taichung mediation is on 22 Oct; demand is 15% of operating profit vs ~2.2% now, Micron's 35-68 months' pay offer was declined. Base rate for Taiwan/Korea chip strikes is that they end in a bonus settlement with little lost output, but headlines skew negative (MU -0.6% on 22 Sep report), so I price a small left skew; (2) Samsung Q3 prelim (~7-8 Oct) and full results (~29-30 Oct), SK hynix Q3 (27/28 Oct), Kioxia (30 Oct): peer read-through on DRAM/HBM pricing, likely confirming tightness; (3) FOMC 27-28 Oct (low hike odds for October; the ~74% December hike odds on Kalshi/Polymarket are sentiment only); (4) late-Oct hyperscaler capex guides. Post-earnings drift after the FQ1 guide beat is small (+0.9% across the print). Net: median at spot (~$1,075), ~21% monthly log-sigma (80% annual / ~3.5), with ~0.01 trimmed off strikes at and above spot for the strike headline risk. Round 1 centred ~1% above spot; I removed that tilt.

fair_value.method: Blend of FY28 consensus EPS $205.95 x 5.0x = $1,030 (50%), mid-cycle EPS $145 x 7.0x = $1,015 (25%), and a cycle-aware DCF with a 2029-30 downturn plus ~$175/sh horizon net cash = $840 (25%); blended ~$980 for Oct 2027, ~9% below spot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Aug-28) consensus EPS $205.95 x 5.0x forward P/E at Oct 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: Yahoo consensus (33 analysts). Kept unchanged: the FQ1 guide was ~8% above consensus so estimates are more likely to drift up near term; the Taiwan profit-sharing risk (a partial move from ~2.2% toward Samsung/SK hynix's ~10% of operating profit) is handled in the scenarios rather than as a haircut.

Core memory peers (SK hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, Nanya, Sandisk) on one NTM basis have a median ~4.7x (range ~4.2-7.8x). MU's own minimum P/E at the last four EPS peaks was 3.5x/8.1x/2.4x/6.1x (mean 5.0x, median 4.8x; Motley Fool, May 2026) and 2018 traded ~4.5x forward (Trefis). 5.0x is ~6% above the core median, within the ~10% premium the SCA floor and US listing can support, and equal to MU's own peak-cycle average.
Midpoint of BofA's history-calibrated bear EPS ~$100 (DRAM ASP -30%, NAND -40%) and the FY27/FY28 consensus average ~$191, rounded.

Round 1 averaged 4.5x (2018) and 11x (2022) forward. The 2022 11x was a forward multiple on collapsing estimates (FQ1 FY23 EPS guided -98%); on trailing peak EPS the 2022 minimum was 6.1x (Motley Fool table). Re-weighting toward peak-EPS-consistent history (2015 8.1x, 2022 6.1x, 2018 ~4.5x forward) and applying to normalized, not peak, EPS gives ~7x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Value at Oct 2027: FCF/share FY28 $155, FY29 $70, FY30 $50, terminal $60 at 12%/2% (PV ~$665) plus net cash ~$175/share

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 consensus EPS $205.95 x ~75% conversion given capex guided above $50B/yr (FQ1 ~$11.5B, 1H ~$25B, 2H higher).
Supply wave 2028-31 (Morningstar via Stocktwits, secondary) and BofA bear EPS ~$100; history shows -40/-60% ASP downturns; FCF lower still on elevated capex.

Cost of equity for a high-beta cyclical: MU's crisis drawdowns average ~2x the S&P (Trefis), i.e. an effective beta ~1.8; ~4.3% risk-free + 1.8 x ~4.3% ERP ~ 12%. No longer derived from the December Fed-hike odds, which are sentiment only.

inputs_detail.input: Net cash per share at Oct 2027
inputs_detail.derivation: FQ4 net cash $68.3B less $12.7B refundable SCA deposits = $55.6B, plus FY27 FCF ~$145-150B (consensus NI ~$203B + ~$12B D&A - ~$55-60B capex) = ~$200B over 1.15B diluted shares (8-K diluted 1,147M). Round 1 double-counted the deposits and used 1.13B basic shares.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market front-runs the 2028-29 supply wave (SK hynix Y1 Feb-27, Samsung P5 1H27, Micron ID1 and Tongluo mid-27, CXMT to ~420k wpm, then Japan/ID2) and/or AI capex digestion; DRAM/NAND price increases stall in 2H27 and a Taiwan profit-sharing settlement lifts costs. As in 2018 (-57% from ~4.5x forward while EPS still rose) and 2022 (-50%), the stock falls ~50% before earnings peak: ~4x a reduced FY28 EPS of ~$140.

base.story: FY27 delivers at or above consensus (FQ1 guide $61.5B/$38.15 is the stated margin floor) and FY28 still looks tight, but the market caps the multiple at MU's own peak-cycle average ~5x FY28 EPS of ~$200-206; net cash builds to ~$175/sh and capital return steps up from 9 Dec 2026. Stock slightly below today with very high path volatility.

bull.story: SCAs (26 deals, ~$150B RPO at floor prices, $32B commitments) persuade investors this cycle is structurally shallower; supply stays short into 2029-30; MU re-rates toward ~7.5x FY28 EPS of ~$220 (the through-cycle multiple applied to peak earnings).

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM (Oct-26 to Sep-27) P/E 4.2x (Kioxia) to 7.8x (Sandisk); NTM EV/EBITDA ~2.5x (Samsung) to ~6.5x (Sandisk). Only five genuine DRAM/NAND manufacturers are listed, so the set is five; HDD makers (WDC, STX), fabless controllers (SIMO, Phison) and small NOR/SLC specialists (Winbond, Macronix) from round 1 are dropped. Round 1's 13.95x 'forward' EV/EBITDA median was trailing (TTM) and is restated on NTM. Multiples from StockAnalysis pages put on one NTM basis per the round-1 supervisor's fiscal-year conversion.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.0x FY28 EPS at the horizon is ~6% above the core NTM median (4.73x) and below MU's current ~6.0x NTM; it equals the mean of MU's own minimum P/E at its last four EPS peaks (5.0x). The 7.0x through-cycle multiple is applied only to normalized EPS.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Only a small premium: the SCA floors (~$150B RPO at minimum prices, deposits) and US listing are documented and persistent, but SK hynix and Samsung also hold long-term HBM/DRAM contracts and large net cash, and history shows peak multiples compress regardless (2018 ~4.5x forward). No sell-side outperformance claim is used.

thesis_break_reason: Rebuilt from post-print numbers (it lands where round 1 did): $600 = FY28 priced as a downturn year at BofA's history-calibrated bear EPS ~$100 x MU's median minimum P/E at past EPS peaks (4.8x) = $480, plus ~$127/sh of FY27 cash build that is largely locked in by the FQ1 guide ($61.5B, stated FY27 margin floor) and SCA floors ($55.6B ex-deposit net cash today -> ~$200B by Oct 2027 on 1.15B shares). Below ~$600 (-44%) the market would be pricing an actual DRAM/HBM contract-price roll-over, SCA renegotiation or an AI-capex cut, not 80%-vol noise; that is the 2018/2022 peak-reversal path (-50% to -57%).

key_uncertainties: Timing of the stock's peak relative to the earnings peak: history says the stock turns 2-3 quarters before EPS, and by Oct 2027 the market will be looking at 2028-29 when new fabs (ID1, Japan, ID2, Singapore NAND, NY) add supply.
Whether SCAs with floor pricing (~$150B RPO) make this cycle structurally shallower than 2018/2022.
Durability of hyperscaler AI capex through 2027.
Rate path: Kalshi and Polymarket price a December 2026 hike near 74% (aggregator snapshots); treated as sentiment, not a valuation input.
Capex inflation (FY27 above $50B implied) reducing FCF and signalling industry overbuild.

Taiwan profit-sharing dispute: unions want 15% of operating profit vs ~2.2%; a settlement toward Samsung/SK hynix's ~10% would trim EPS by a few percent, a strike would hit ~60% of output including HBM.
reasoning: Base-rate anchor unchanged: every prior memory boom ended in a 50-70% drawdown (2014-16 -70%, 2018 -57% from ~4.5x forward while EPS still rose, 2022 -50%), the stock leads earnings by 2-3 quarters, and MU's minimum P/E at its last four EPS peaks averaged 5.0x (3.5/8.1/2.4/6.1). Fundamentals are the strongest ever (FQ4 $54.2B, FQ1 guide $61.5B/$38.15 ~8% above consensus, 26 SCAs with ~$150B RPO, $68.3B net cash). Round-2 corrections from the supervisor: (1) horizon net cash cut from ~$198 to ~$175/sh (deposits were double-counted, diluted 1.15B shares), lowering the DCF to $840; (2) the 2022 11x was a forward multiple on collapsing estimates (trailing minimum 6.1x), so the through-cycle multiple drops from 8x to 7x, mid-cycle leg $1,015; (3) the 12% discount rate is now built from MU's ~2x-market drawdown beta, not the December hike odds (re-checked: Kalshi 73.5%, Polymarket 74%, but sentiment only); (4) peers cut to the five core DRAM/NAND makers on an NTM basis (median ~4.7x) and EV/EBITDA restated from trailing 13.95x to NTM ~3.5x. I keep FY28 consensus $205.95 (the supervisor's ~$200 is close; the guide beat argues against a haircut) and 5.0x, which both peers and MU's own history support. Fair value ~$980 (was $1,020). Scenarios bear $560 (30%), base $1,000 (45%), bull $1,650 (25%); mean ~$1,030, median ~$985. The ladder blends the scenario mixture with a ~65% log-vol lognormal around ~$975, keeping the fat left tail (P<$537 ~16%) and thinning the far right tail slightly. New in-window risk: the confirmed Taiwan strike vote. Research limits: Livewire and Nasdaq history pages returned 403/503; 6 follow-up searches/fetches.
